name: Zenfolio
tagline: Publish a portfolio and client galleries with basic downloads

pricing.notes: Typical Portfolio monthly tier with annual billing.

tiers.name: Portfolio
tiers.limits: 15 GB storage (about 4,500 photos) and 500 SMS messages per month.
tiers.notes: The displayed annual-equivalent price appears to be a first-year offer scheduled to end August 15, 2026; renewal price was not disclosed.

tiers.name: PortfolioPlus
tiers.limits: 150 GB storage (about 60,000 photos) and 2,500 SMS messages per month.
tiers.notes: The displayed annual-equivalent price appears to be a first-year offer scheduled to end August 15, 2026; renewal price was not disclosed.

tiers.name: ProSuite
tiers.limits: Unlimited JPEG photo storage; 150 GB video (about 10 hours); 5,000 SMS messages per month; up to 4K video.
tiers.notes: The displayed annual-equivalent price appears to be a first-year offer scheduled to end August 15, 2026; renewal price was not disclosed.

pricing.freeTierCaps: no free tier; a free trial is offered, but the current live page did not reliably expose its numeric duration
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual; displayed annual rates are promotional first-year equivalents
pricing.hiddenCosts: AI culling is $7/month on Portfolio and PortfolioPlus; Booking is $10/month on those tiers; RAW storage above 2 GB is $0.085/GB/month; commerce carries a 7% platform fee plus payment processing; terms also set 100 GB/month bandwidth and 25 GB/gallery limits.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Zenfolio, publish a portfolio and client galleries with basic downloads. The hard boundary is hosting, templates, proofing, commerce, print labs, and photographer support, plus image pipeline quality, models, and workflow polish.
coreLoopDIY: Catalog local photos, generate previews, apply non-destructive adjustments, publish a portfolio and client galleries with basic downloads, and export selected originals or rendered copies.
whatYouLose: hosting, templates, proofing, commerce, print labs, and photographer support
moatNotes: image pipeline quality, models, and workflow polish
ongoingBurden: raw codecs, color management, metadata, previews, face models, GPU support, storage, backups, sync, and export fidelity
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Zenfolio because photographers pay because image quality, catalog safety, and fast handling of huge libraries matter more than cloning sliders. The recurring cost buys raw codecs, color management, metadata, previews, face models, GPU support, storage, backups, sync, and export fidelity, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Immich
priorArt.desc: Active open-source self-hosted photo and video management platform.

alternatives.name: Lychee
alternatives.desc: A tidy self-hosted portfolio and passworded client gallery with downloads; deliberately light on business machinery.

facts.install: Docker Compose with the Lychee image and MariaDB; prebuilt and source installs also exist
facts.dataFormat: Uploaded originals and derivatives live in persistent uploads storage; albums, users, metadata and settings live in MariaDB (or another configured database), with separate logs and temporary-data volumes
facts.gapVsPaid: It handles portfolios and private downloads but lacks Zenfolio's client proofing, store, print fulfillment, booking and photographer-business automation.
facts.setupBlocker: Docker Compose, writable persistent volumes, a database, an APP_KEY, and domain/TLS setup for remote sharing

alternatives.name: Photoview
alternatives.desc: Turns owned folders into a clean web portfolio with RAW, EXIF, users, shares, and downloads; design customization is sparse.

facts.install: Docker Compose with SQLite, MariaDB, or PostgreSQL and one or more mounted media folders
facts.engines: Built-in dlib/go-face face detection and recognition; FFmpeg for video processing; optional Mapbox token for maps
facts.dataFormat: Original photos remain in the mounted folder tree; the database stores users, albums, indexes, and face metadata, while a media-cache directory stores thumbnails and optimized video
facts.gapVsPaid: Its design customization is sparse and it has none of Zenfolio's commerce, proofing, booking, marketing or managed-domain workflow.
facts.setupBlocker: Docker plus careful volume paths and host-file permissions; safe remote access also needs a reverse proxy or VPN and TLS

alternatives.name: Piwigo
alternatives.desc: Portfolio-like themes, private client albums, users, metadata, and downloads on your server; sales and lab fulfillment do not come along.

facts.install: Upload the NetInstall script or release to PHP web hosting, then complete browser setup against MySQL or MariaDB
facts.dataFormat: Originals live under the upload or galleries directories, generated derivatives and configuration stay in the Piwigo tree, and albums, users, metadata, and plugin state live in MySQL or MariaDB
facts.gapVsPaid: It can build a portfolio through themes and plugins, but sales, lab fulfillment, proofing and photographer-business automation remain separate projects.
facts.setupBlocker: Requires PHP web hosting, a database, writable directories, and ongoing web-server, TLS, and plugin maintenance

rejectedAlternatives.name: Immich
rejectedAlternatives.desc: A strong personal archive with sharing, not a purpose-built portfolio and client-delivery surface.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Portfolio plan and a personal local photo catalog DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Zenfolio in an empty repository.
Use Tauri 2, React, TypeScript, Rust image libraries, SQLite, and local filesystem access; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: catalog local photos, generate previews, apply non-destructive adjustments, publish a portfolio and client galleries with basic downloads, and export selected originals or rendered copies.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Index selected folders without moving or rewriting originals and store only catalog data in SQLite.
Generate thumbnails and previews, read EXIF, detect duplicates by hash, and monitor file changes.
Provide timeline, folders, albums, ratings, flags, tags, search, and side-by-side compare.
Store edits as reversible parameters for crop, rotate, exposure, contrast, white balance, and saturation.
Render exports to a new folder with explicit color space, quality, size, and metadata choices.
Add catalog backup, missing-file repair, integrity scan, and a clear original-safety guarantee.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out a proprietary raw-rendering engine.
Deliberately leave out hosted cross-device photo sync and client galleries.
Deliberately leave out frontier culling, retouching, and generative models.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
